                                        Day-1

# 🔹 Core JPA Annotations

### `@Entity`

* Marks the class as a **JPA entity**
* Hibernate creates a **table** with the same name (default: class name)

```java
@Entity
public class Product { }
```

---

### `@Id`

* Marks the **primary key** of the table

```java
@Id
private Long id;
```

---

### `@GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)`

* Database generates the ID (auto-increment)
* Uses MySQL’s `AUTO_INCREMENT`

✔ Best choice for MySQL

---

### Lombok Annotations (Not JPA)

```java
@Getter @Setter
@AllArgsConstructor
@NoArgsConstructor
```

* Generate getters/setters & constructors at compile time
* Reduce boilerplate code
* **No DB impact**

---

# 🔹 Relationship Annotations (Most Important Part)

## 1️⃣ `@ManyToOne` (Product → Category)

```java
@ManyToOne(cascade = CascadeType.ALL)
@JoinColumn(name = "category_id")
private Category category;
```

### 🔹 What does `@ManyToOne` mean?

* **Many products belong to one category**
* This side **owns the relationship**
* Database has a **foreign key column**

📌 Table structure:

```sql
product
-------
id
name
category_id  ← foreign key
```

---

### 🔹 Why `@JoinColumn`?

```java
@JoinColumn(name = "category_id")
```

* Specifies the **foreign key column**
* Without it, Hibernate uses:

  ```text
  category_id (default)
  ```

---

### 🔹 What does `cascade = CascadeType.ALL` do?

Cascade means:
👉 *What happens to Product also happens to Category*

| Cascade   | Effect                                  |
| --------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `PERSIST` | Save category when product saved        |
| `MERGE`   | Update category when product updated    |
| `REMOVE`  | ❌ Deletes category when product deleted |
| `ALL`     | Includes everything                     |

⚠️ **Danger here**:
If you delete a product → **category also gets deleted**, even if other products use it.

❌ **Bad practice for `ManyToOne`**

✅ Better:

```java
@ManyToOne
@JoinColumn(name = "category_id")
private Category category;
```

---

## 2️⃣ `@OneToMany` (Category → Product)

```java
@OneToMany(mappedBy = "category")
private List<Product> products;
```

### 🔹 What does `@OneToMany` mean?

* **One category has many products**
* This is the **inverse (non-owning) side**
* No foreign key here

---

### 🔹 What is `mappedBy`?

```java
mappedBy = "category"
```

* Points to the **field name in Product**

```java
private Category category;
```

Meaning:

> “The `Product.category` field owns the relationship.”

📌 Result:

* No extra column
* No extra join table
* Clean schema

❌ Without `mappedBy`, Hibernate creates:

```sql
category_products (extra join table)
```

---

## 3️⃣ `@OneToMany` (Product → Image)

```java
@OneToMany(mappedBy = "product",
           cascade = CascadeType.ALL,
           orphanRemoval = true)
private List<Image> images;
```

### 🔹 Meaning

* One product has **many images**
* Image table holds the foreign key

---

### 🔹 `mappedBy = "product"`

* Relationship owned by:

```java
Image.product
```

---

### 🔹 `cascade = CascadeType.ALL`

* Save product → images saved
* Delete product → images deleted
* Update product → images updated

✅ **Correct usage here**

---

### 🔹 `orphanRemoval = true`

* If an image is removed from the list:

```java
product.getImages().remove(img);
```

➡️ Image is **deleted from DB**

Used for **dependent child entities**

---

## 4️⃣ `@ManyToOne` (Image → Product)

```java
@ManyToOne
@JoinColumn(name = "product_id")
private Product product;
```

### 🔹 Meaning

* Many images belong to **one product**
* Image owns the relationship

📌 DB:

```sql
image
-----
id
product_id  ← FK
```

---

# 🔹 Other Important Annotations

### `@Lob`

```java
@Lob
private Blob image;
```

* Stores **large binary data**
* Maps to:

  * `BLOB` (MySQL)
  * `BYTEA` (PostgreSQL)

⚠️ For real apps, better store images in:

* File system
* AWS S3
  and save only URL in DB

---

# 🔹 Relationship Ownership Summary

| Relationship       | Owner   |
| ------------------ | ------- |
| Product → Category | Product |
| Category → Product | Product |
| Product → Image    | Image   |
| Image → Product    | Image   |

👉 **Owner = side with `@JoinColumn`**

---

# 🔹 Recommended Fixes (Important)

### ❌ Problem

```java
@ManyToOne(cascade = CascadeType.ALL)
```

### ✅ Correct Version

```java
@ManyToOne
@JoinColumn(name = "category_id")
private Category category;
```

---

# 🔹 Final Conceptual Rule (Remember This)

> 🔹 `@ManyToOne` → FK lives here
> 🔹 `mappedBy` → “I am NOT the owner”
> 🔹 `cascade` → propagates operations
> 🔹 `orphanRemoval` → deletes detached children

---




                                                    Day - 2
## 🔹 Application Identity

### `spring.application.name=dream-shops`

* Sets the **name of your Spring Boot application**.
* Used in:

  * Logs
  * Spring Cloud / Microservices
  * Actuator endpoints
* Helpful when multiple services are running.

---

## 🔹 Server Configuration

### `spring.port=123456` ❌ **(Invalid)**

* ❗ This property is **wrong**.
* Correct property:

  ```properties
  server.port=8080
  ```
* Port range must be **0–65535**
* `123456` exceeds the maximum allowed value.

✅ **Fix**

```properties
server.port=8080
```

---

## 🔹 Database Connection (MySQL)

### `spring.datasource.url=jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/dream-shops`

* JDBC URL for connecting to **MySQL**
* Components:

  * `localhost` → database host
  * `3306` → default MySQL port
  * `dream-shops` → database name

---

### `spring.datasource.username=root`

* MySQL **username** used by Spring Boot to connect to DB.

---

### `spring.datasource.password=root`

* Password for the above MySQL user.
* ⚠️ Avoid hard-coding passwords in production.

---

### `spring.datasource.driver-class-name=com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver`

* MySQL JDBC **driver class**
* Required to allow Java to talk to MySQL.
* `cj` = Connector/J (newer driver).

---

## 🔹 Hibernate / JPA Configuration

### `spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.dialect=org.hibernate.dialect.MySQLDialect`

* Tells Hibernate **which SQL dialect** to generate.
* Ensures compatibility with MySQL syntax.

👉 For newer MySQL versions, better:

```properties
org.hibernate.dialect.MySQL8Dialect
```

---

### `spring.jpa.show-sql=true`

* Prints **generated SQL queries** in the console.
* Very useful for debugging and learning.

---

### `spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.format_sql=true`

* Formats SQL queries to be **readable** (line breaks & indentation).
* Works together with `show-sql`.

---

### `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=update`

* Controls **automatic schema generation**.

| Value         | Meaning                                |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `none`        | No DB changes                          |
| `create`      | Drops & creates tables on startup      |
| `create-drop` | Creates on start, drops on shutdown    |
| `update`      | Updates schema without deleting data ✅ |
| `validate`    | Checks schema only                     |

⚠️ `update` is fine for development, **not recommended in production**.

---

## ✅ Corrected Version (Recommended)

```properties
spring.application.name=dream-shops

server.port=8080

spring.datasource.url=jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/dream-shops
spring.datasource.username=root
spring.datasource.password=root
spring.datasource.driver-class-name=com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver

spring.jpa.database-platform=org.hibernate.dialect.MySQL8Dialect
spring.jpa.show-sql=true
spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.format_sql=true
spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=update
```

---
